misconceptions: self-belief requires thinking others are inferior

words.sense: acting as though you are superior to others
misconceptions: speaking with certainty is always arrogance

semantic_axes.description: whether self-belief includes a claim of superiority

edges.boundary_rule: Confidence trusts your own ability; arrogance assumes you are above other people.

beats.text: Ari believes she can handle the presentation after practising it carefully.
beats.reason: Her belief rests on preparation, with no claim that other people are inferior.

hints.attention: What does Ari say about the other people?
hints.axis: Separate belief in yourself from contempt for others.
hints.contrast: Being sure you can succeed does not require putting anyone else down.

beats.text: She also says nobody else on the team is capable of doing it properly.
beats.decisive_clue: nobody else on the team is capable
beats.reason: Dismissing everyone else introduces superiority; self-belief alone no longer captures her attitude.

hints.attention: What does Ari say about the other people?
hints.axis: Separate belief in yourself from contempt for others.
hints.contrast: Being sure you can succeed does not require putting anyone else down.

beats.text: Even when a teammate offers a useful improvement, Ari says their ideas are beneath her.
beats.reason: The new detail reinforces contempt for teammates rather than simply trust in her own ability.

hints.attention: What does Ari say about the other people?
hints.axis: Separate belief in yourself from contempt for others.
hints.contrast: Being sure you can succeed does not require putting anyone else down.

chains.feedback_short: One detail changed the meaning: Ari put everyone else below her.
chains.feedback_deep: The first statement concerned Ari’s own preparation. Dismissing teammates introduced superiority. Speaking to a large audience does not remove that claim.
chains.contrast_rule: Confidence trusts your own ability; arrogance assumes you are above other people.

beats.text: Sam tells the band, “I have practised my part and I can do this.”
beats.reason: Sam trusts preparation without claiming superiority.

hints.attention: Did Sam put anybody else down?
hints.axis: Focus on respect for others, not audience size.
hints.contrast: Believing you can handle pressure is different from considering others beneath you.

beats.text: The band learns the audience will be much larger; Sam still believes the practice will be enough.
beats.reason: The larger audience adds pressure, not contempt for anyone else.

hints.attention: Did Sam put anybody else down?

hints.contrast: Believing you can handle pressure is different from considering others beneath you.

beats.text: Sam says this firmly, then thanks a bandmate for a useful suggestion.
beats.decisive_clue: thanks a bandmate for a useful suggestion
beats.reason: A firm manner coexists with respect; there is no claim of superiority.

chains.feedback_short: A bigger audience changes the pressure, not Sam’s respect for other people.
chains.feedback_deep: The audience grows and Sam speaks firmly, but still respects a teammate’s contribution. Neither detail implies superiority.
